ITID-71111.def: An operational support request, submitted via the ServiceNow ticketing channel, asking the SOC or IAM team to unlock a locked-out account.
ITID-71111.purpose: Captures a ServiceNow ticket requesting that a locked account be unlocked or that a triggered risk signal be dismissed as a false positive.
scopeIncludes: Account lockout following repeated failed login attempts
Lockout following a triggered conditional-access or risk policy
scopeExcludes: The underlying risk signal or lockout cause itself (tracked under the relevant detection ITID)
Requests submitted via IM or email (sibling ITIDs under those channels)
ITID-71111.severity: Low under normal circumstances; escalate to Medium if the requester's identity cannot be readily verified or the lockout followed a genuine risk signal.
ITID-71111.priority: P4 routine; P3 if the requester is blocked from performing a business-critical function.
ITID-71111.escalation: Escalate to the SOC analyst on duty if the account was locked due to a real detection (not a routine failed-login lockout) before unlocking.
indicators: ServiceNow ticket category 'Account Unlock'
Requester citing repeated login failures or an unexpected block
vectors: An attacker impersonating the account owner to request an unlock and regain access — verify identity before acting
rootCauses: Forgotten password leading to repeated failed attempts
Legitimate but unusual login pattern triggering a risk-based lockout
controls: Identity verification step before any unlock action
Audit logging of all unlock actions with requester and approver identity
ITID-71111.detection: This is an intake classification for a support request, not a detection; the underlying lockout trigger has its own detection coverage.
ITID-71111.response: Verify the requester's identity through an out-of-band channel before unlocking; check the lockout reason before dismissing it as routine.
metrics: Unlock requests processed per week
Median time to resolve an unlock ticket
ITID-71111.notes: If investigation reveals the lockout was caused by a genuine compromise attempt, reclassify the underlying event under the appropriate credential-access ITID rather than leaving it here.

playbook.name: Account Lockout Unlock Request
playbook.description: ServiceNow-ticketed request to unlock a user account that has been locked out, handled as a verified change-management action rather than an attack investigation.

steps.title: Review ServiceNow ticket and confirm portal authentication
steps.desc: Open the ServiceNow ticket and confirm it was submitted through the authenticated employee portal under the requestor's own logged-in identity.
steps.guidance: Portal login provides baseline assurance, but still confirm the ticket's submitter field matches the account owner or an authorized delegate (e.g. manager, helpdesk agent acting on the user's behalf).
steps.outcome: Ticket is confirmed as submitted by an authenticated, identifiable requestor.
steps.abort: If the ticket shows signs of being submitted through a shared or generic portal account, escalate to identity team before proceeding.

steps.title: Verify requestor is authorized for the locked account
steps.desc: Confirm the person requesting the unlock is either the account owner or has documented delegate/manager authority over that account.
steps.guidance: Cross-check requestor identity against HR/AD record for the target account; do not unlock third-party accounts on a colleague's say-so without delegate documentation.
steps.outcome: Requestor-to-account relationship is confirmed and documented in the ticket.
steps.abort: If requestor cannot be tied to the account, reject the request and direct them to submit via the account owner or HR.

steps.title: Determine lockout cause
steps.desc: Check the authentication/security logs to determine why the account was locked (repeated bad password attempts, policy trigger, active risk alert, admin lock).
steps.guidance: If the lockout correlates with a live risk/impossible-travel alert, treat this as a possible compromised-account scenario, not a routine unlock.
steps.outcome: Lockout root cause is identified and recorded on the ticket.
steps.abort: If lockout is tied to an active, unresolved risk detection, halt the unlock and escalate to the on-call analyst for compromise triage.

steps.title: Confirm account remains locked pending verification
steps.desc: Note in the ticket that the account remains in its locked state while identity and cause checks are completed, preventing premature access.
steps.guidance: This is a holding step only — no action is taken on the account yet.
steps.outcome: Account lock state is confirmed unchanged and documented pending eradication step.

steps.title: Unlock the account
steps.desc: Perform the account unlock in Active Directory / IAM once identity and cause checks pass.
steps.guidance: Use the standard unlock procedure; do not reset the password unless the user also reports a forgotten password.
steps.abort: If unlock action fails or triggers a secondary alert, stop and escalate to IAM administrators.

steps.title: Confirm user can authenticate
steps.desc: Ask the requestor/user to attempt login, or confirm via monitoring that a successful authentication event follows the unlock.
steps.guidance: A successful login event within a reasonable window confirms the unlock was effective.
steps.abort: If login still fails, re-check for a secondary lock source (conditional access, MFA lock) before re-escalating.

steps.title: Close ticket and notify requestor
steps.desc: Update the ServiceNow ticket with actions taken and outcome, then close it and notify the requestor.
steps.guidance: Include the lockout cause and unlock time for audit trail.
steps.outcome: Ticket closed with full audit trail.

steps.title: Track recurring lockouts for this account/user
steps.desc: If this account or user has multiple lockout tickets in a short period, flag for a deeper review of password hygiene, MFA setup, or targeted credential attack.
steps.guidance: Recurring lockouts can indicate a password-spray target or a broken MFA/SSO integration.
steps.outcome: Recurrence pattern documented; escalated for deeper review if threshold exceeded.

ITID-71112.def: A support request submitted via ServiceNow to have a specific triggered risk or security alert reviewed and cleared without further action.
ITID-71112.purpose: Captures a ServiceNow ticket asking the SOC to review and dismiss a security alert believed to be a false positive.
scopeIncludes: Requests to dismiss a flagged sign-in risk
Requests to clear a DLP or endpoint alert believed to be benign
scopeExcludes: The alert itself, which retains its own detection/ITID classification regardless of outcome
Bulk policy-tuning requests to reduce false positives generally (a different Miscellaneous Requests leaf)
ITID-71112.severity: Low; treat as routine triage unless the alert in question was independently corroborated by other signals.
ITID-71112.priority: P4, processed in normal SOC triage queue order.
ITID-71112.escalation: Escalate to a senior analyst before dismissal if the alert correlates with any other open investigation.
indicators: ServiceNow ticket referencing a specific alert ID
Requester providing business justification for the flagged activity
vectors: An adversary or insider pressuring an analyst to dismiss a genuine detection under the guise of a false-positive request
rootCauses: Overly sensitive detection rule thresholds
Legitimate but atypical user behavior (e.g., travel, new device)
controls: Two-person review for dismissal of alerts tied to privileged accounts
Retention of dismissed-alert rationale for audit
ITID-71112.detection: This ITID classifies the dismissal request itself; the originating alert has its own detection coverage.
ITID-71112.response: Re-verify the underlying alert evidence independently before dismissing; do not dismiss solely on requester assertion.
metrics: False-positive dismissal rate by alert type
Analyst time spent per dismissal review
ITID-71112.notes: A pattern of frequent dismissal requests for the same alert type should trigger a detection-tuning review rather than repeated manual dismissal.

playbook.name: False-Positive Risk Alert Dismissal Request
playbook.description: ServiceNow-ticketed request to dismiss a user-risk or sign-in-risk alert as a false positive, requiring independent confirmation before dismissal.

steps.title: Review ServiceNow ticket and confirm portal authentication
steps.desc: Confirm the dismissal request was submitted through the authenticated portal by the account owner or an authorized delegate.
steps.guidance: Check the submitter identity against the affected user/account referenced in the risk alert.
steps.abort: If unauthorized, reject and redirect to proper channel.

steps.title: Independently review the underlying risk alert
steps.desc: Pull the original risk detection (e.g. impossible travel, anomalous sign-in, leaked credential) and review the raw evidence yourself rather than accepting the requestor's claim at face value.
steps.guidance: Do not dismiss solely because the user says 'that was me' — check IP/geo, device fingerprint, and timing against known user travel/behavior.
steps.outcome: Analyst has independently formed a judgment on whether the alert is a genuine false positive.
steps.abort: If evidence is ambiguous or suggests genuine compromise, do not dismiss — escalate to incident response instead.

steps.title: Gather corroborating context
steps.desc: Collect supporting detail such as VPN usage, known travel, or device enrollment that explains the anomaly.
steps.guidance: Document the specific explanation, not just 'confirmed false positive'.
steps.outcome: Explanation for the anomaly is documented on the ticket.

steps.title: Confirm risk flag/restriction remains in place pending review
steps.desc: Ensure any interim restriction (e.g. blocked sign-in, forced MFA) tied to the risk alert stays active until the review is complete.
steps.guidance: No premature clearing of the risk state.
steps.outcome: Interim restriction confirmed unchanged pending eradication.

steps.title: Dismiss the risk alert / clear the risk state
steps.desc: In the identity risk platform, mark the alert as confirmed-safe and clear the associated user risk level.
steps.guidance: Use the platform's 'confirmed safe' dismissal reason, not 'ignore', to preserve accurate telemetry for future risk scoring.
steps.outcome: Risk alert dismissed and user risk level cleared.
steps.abort: If dismissal option is unavailable or requires higher privilege, escalate to identity security team.

steps.title: Confirm normal access restored
steps.desc: Verify the user can sign in normally without the risk-based restriction re-triggering.
steps.outcome: User authenticates normally with no residual restriction.
steps.abort: If restriction persists, check for a separate conditional-access policy still applying.

steps.title: Close ticket and notify requestor
steps.desc: Document the dismissal rationale and evidence reviewed, then close the ticket and notify the requestor.

steps.title: Track false-positive rate for the triggering detection rule
steps.desc: Log this dismissal against the specific detection rule so recurring false positives can be identified for tuning.
steps.guidance: If a rule generates a high false-positive rate for a given population (e.g. frequent travelers), recommend threshold or scoping tuning to the detection engineering team.
steps.outcome: False-positive instance logged; tuning recommendation raised if pattern threshold met.

ITID-71113.def: A general classification for account-unlock or risk-dismissal support tickets submitted via ServiceNow that lack a more specific categorization.
ITID-71113.purpose: Intake bucket for ServiceNow password-unlock or risk-dismissal requests that do not fit the more specific sibling leaves.
scopeIncludes: Any ServiceNow unlock/dismissal request not otherwise classified
scopeExcludes: Requests clearly matching ITID-71111 (unlock) or ITID-71112 (risk dismissal)
ITID-71113.severity: Low by default; reassess once the specific nature of the request is known.
ITID-71113.escalation: Reclassify to a specific sibling ITID once triaged; escalate only if evidence of compromise emerges.
indicators: ServiceNow ticket that does not cleanly match the unlock or dismissal templates
vectors: Same social-engineering risk as the specific sibling leaves — verify identity before acting
rootCauses: Ambiguous or incomplete ticket submission
controls: Identity verification before any account action
Mandatory reclassification during triage
ITID-71113.detection: Intake classification only; not a detection.
ITID-71113.response: Triage promptly and reclassify to the specific applicable ITID.
metrics: Volume of unclassified requests requiring re-triage
ITID-71113.notes: This leaf should see declining volume over time as intake triage improves; persistent high volume suggests the intake form needs better categorization options.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Password Unlock or Risk Dismissal Request
playbook.description: ServiceNow-ticketed catch-all request related to password unlock or risk dismissal that does not fit a more specific subtype.

steps.title: Review ticket and classify the actual request
steps.desc: Read the ServiceNow ticket in full and determine which specific action is actually being requested (unlock, risk dismissal, password reset, or something else) since it was routed as unclassified.
steps.guidance: Re-categorize the ticket to a specific type where possible for future reporting; proceed generically only if it truly doesn't fit.
steps.outcome: Request is understood in concrete, actionable terms.
steps.abort: If the request is out of scope for this team, reroute to the correct queue.

steps.title: Confirm portal authentication and requestor authorization
steps.desc: Confirm the requestor is authenticated via the portal and authorized to act on the target account.
steps.guidance: Cross-check against AD/HR records for account ownership or delegate authority.
steps.abort: Reject if authorization cannot be established.

steps.title: Gather account and justification specifics
steps.desc: Collect the exact account identifier and business justification needed to act.
steps.outcome: Ticket contains sufficient detail to execute the action.
steps.abort: If insufficient detail is provided, return the ticket to the requestor for clarification.

steps.title: Confirm current account state before change
steps.desc: Record the account's current lock/risk state so the change can be verified afterward.

steps.title: Execute the appropriate unlock or dismissal action
steps.desc: Perform the specific action identified in step 1 (unlock account, dismiss risk, or both) using the appropriate console.
steps.abort: If the action fails or is not supported, escalate to IAM/identity security.

steps.title: Verify resolution
steps.desc: Confirm the account now behaves as expected (user can log in, risk indicator cleared).
steps.abort: If unresolved, re-open investigation into root cause.

steps.title: Close ticket and notify requestor
steps.desc: Document actions taken and close the ticket.

steps.title: Flag for intake template improvement if miscategorized frequently
steps.desc: If unclassified tickets of this shape recur, recommend adding a specific ServiceNow catalog item so future requests route directly to the correct playbook.

ITID-71121.def: A support ticket requesting that a specific endpoint be network-isolated or quarantined, typically as a precautionary or investigative containment action.
ITID-71121.purpose: Captures a ServiceNow request to isolate an endpoint from the network due to suspected compromise.
scopeIncludes: Requests from an analyst or manager to isolate a device pending investigation
Requests triggered by a user reporting suspicious device behavior
scopeExcludes: The underlying suspected-compromise incident, which carries its own ITID classification
Automated EDR-triggered isolation (a distinct detection/response action, not a ticket request)
ITID-71121.severity: Medium to High, since containment requests generally imply an active or suspected security concern.
ITID-71121.priority: P2, processed ahead of routine tickets given the containment intent.
ITID-71121.escalation: Escalate immediately to the SOC on-call analyst; containment requests should not wait in a routine queue.
indicators: ServiceNow ticket flagged as urgent/containment
Reference to a specific hostname or asset tag
vectors: An adversary attempting to trigger unnecessary isolation of a legitimate/critical system as a denial-of-service distraction
rootCauses: Genuine suspected malware or intrusion on the device
User-reported anomalous behavior later found benign
controls: Rapid-isolation capability via EDR
Verification of requester authority to request containment
ITID-71121.detection: Intake classification for the containment request; the suspected compromise itself is tracked under its own ITID.
ITID-71121.response: Isolate promptly, then open or link to the corresponding investigation ITID for the suspected compromise.
metrics: Time from containment request to isolation completed
Percentage of containment requests confirmed as true positives
ITID-71121.notes: Always link this ticket to the underlying incident ITID once identified, so containment action and root cause remain traceable together.

playbook.name: Endpoint Isolation Request (Suspected Compromise)
playbook.description: ServiceNow-ticketed request to isolate an endpoint suspected of compromise, which may itself be the start of a full security incident.

steps.title: Review ticket and confirm portal authentication
steps.desc: Confirm the request was submitted through the authenticated portal by an authorized requestor (device owner, IT support, or security analyst).
steps.abort: Reject if requestor cannot be authenticated.

steps.title: Gather compromise indicators and device details
steps.desc: Collect the specific device identifier, hostname, and the indicators that led to the suspected-compromise claim.
steps.guidance: Request any available evidence (alert ID, unusual behavior description, EDR detection) rather than isolating on vague suspicion alone.
steps.outcome: Concrete device identity and supporting evidence documented.
steps.abort: If no credible indicator exists, consider treating as a lower-priority general containment request instead.

steps.title: Decide whether to open a full security incident in parallel
steps.desc: Assess whether the reported indicators meet the threshold for opening a formal security incident alongside the containment ticket, rather than treating this purely as a routine request.
steps.guidance: This ticket type is often the START of a real incident. If evidence suggests active compromise (e.g. EDR malware detection, C2 beacon, lateral movement signs), open a parallel incident record and loop in the incident response team; do not just mechanically isolate and close.
steps.outcome: A documented decision is made and recorded: either 'routine containment only' or 'parallel security incident opened, ref #___'.

steps.title: Confirm current containment status of the device
steps.desc: Check whether the device is already isolated, partially restricted, or fully on-network before making a change.
steps.outcome: Current containment state confirmed and documented.

steps.title: Isolate the endpoint
steps.desc: Apply network isolation to the device via the EDR platform.
steps.guidance: Use full isolation unless a specific exception (e.g. maintain a management channel) is documented.
steps.abort: If isolation fails or the agent is offline, escalate to the endpoint team for out-of-band containment (e.g. network ACL/switch port disable).

steps.title: Verify isolation took effect
steps.desc: Confirm via EDR console and/or network telemetry that the device is no longer able to communicate except with the EDR management plane.
steps.abort: If device still shows network activity, re-attempt isolation or escalate.

steps.title: Close ticket and notify requestor/incident lead
steps.desc: Update the ticket with isolation confirmation; if a parallel incident was opened, hand off ongoing tracking to the incident record and notify the incident lead.
steps.outcome: Ticket closed or linked to the open incident with clear ownership.

steps.title: Review whether isolation request intake captured enough evidence
steps.desc: Note whether the initial ticket had enough detail to make the containment/incident decision quickly, and recommend intake template changes if not.

ITID-71122.def: A support ticket requesting that network isolation on a previously contained endpoint be lifted, typically once investigation or remediation has concluded.
ITID-71122.purpose: Captures a ServiceNow request to release a previously contained/isolated device back to the network.
scopeIncludes: Requests to release isolation after remediation is confirmed complete
Requests to release isolation after investigation concludes the device was not compromised
scopeExcludes: The original containment request (ITID-71121)
The remediation work itself, tracked under the relevant incident ITID
ITID-71122.severity: Low to Medium; the risk lies in releasing a device prematurely before remediation is verified.
ITID-71122.priority: P3, processed promptly to restore business function once verified safe.
ITID-71122.escalation: Escalate to the investigating analyst for sign-off before release if the original containment was tied to a confirmed incident.
indicators: ServiceNow ticket referencing an existing containment case
Confirmation of remediation steps completed
vectors: An attacker still present on the device attempting to have containment lifted prematurely through social engineering of the requester
rootCauses: Successful remediation of a confirmed incident
Determination that the original containment was a false positive
controls: Mandatory sign-off from the investigating analyst before release
Post-release monitoring for a defined observation window
ITID-71122.detection: Intake classification for the release request; not itself a detection.
ITID-71122.response: Confirm remediation evidence before releasing; apply a short post-release monitoring window.
metrics: Time contained before release
Recurrence rate of incidents on released devices
ITID-71122.notes: Never release solely on requester assertion — require explicit sign-off tied to the original containment case record.

playbook.name: Device Containment Release/Reinstatement Request
playbook.description: ServiceNow-ticketed request to release a previously isolated device back onto the network.

steps.title: Review ticket and confirm portal authentication
steps.desc: Confirm the release request was submitted through the authenticated portal by an authorized requestor.
steps.guidance: Verify requestor authority to request release — typically IT support, device owner, or the analyst who handled the original isolation.
steps.abort: Reject if unauthorized.

steps.title: Confirm remediation is complete before release
steps.desc: Check whether the original reason for isolation (malware, investigation, etc.) has been resolved or closed out, and whether any linked security incident has cleared this device for release.
steps.guidance: Do not release a device solely because a user is inconvenienced; confirm with the incident owner if one exists.
steps.outcome: Confirmation obtained that remediation/investigation is complete or the linked incident authorizes release.
steps.abort: If remediation is not confirmed complete, hold the request and escalate to the incident owner.

steps.title: Confirm requestor is authorized for this specific device
steps.desc: Verify the requestor has ownership or delegated authority over the specific device being released, not just general IT/helpdesk standing.
steps.guidance: Cross-check the device asset record for its assigned owner or business unit before releasing.
steps.abort: If the requestor cannot be tied to the device, escalate to the asset owner or device inventory team.

steps.title: Confirm current isolation status of the device
steps.desc: Verify the device is currently isolated before attempting release, to avoid acting on stale ticket data.

steps.title: Release the device from isolation
steps.desc: Remove the network isolation restriction via the EDR platform.
steps.abort: If the release action fails, escalate to endpoint team.

steps.title: Verify device is reachable and behaving normally
steps.desc: Confirm the device can reach normal network resources and shows no recurrence of the original suspicious activity.
steps.guidance: Consider a short monitoring window post-release before fully closing.
steps.outcome: Device confirmed reachable with no recurrence of prior indicators.
steps.abort: If suspicious activity recurs, re-isolate immediately and escalate.

steps.title: Close ticket and notify requestor
steps.desc: Document release rationale and timing, then close the ticket and notify the requestor.

steps.title: Confirm isolation-to-release cycle time was reasonable
steps.desc: Note the total time the device spent isolated and flag if process delays (e.g. missing incident linkage) extended it unnecessarily.
steps.outcome: Cycle time reviewed; process note logged if needed.

ITID-71123.def: A general classification for containment-related support tickets submitted via ServiceNow that lack a more specific categorization.
ITID-71123.purpose: Intake bucket for ServiceNow device-containment requests that do not fit the isolation or release sibling leaves.
scopeIncludes: Any ServiceNow containment-related request not otherwise classified
scopeExcludes: Requests clearly matching ITID-71121 (isolation) or ITID-71122 (release)
ITID-71123.severity: Medium by default given the containment context; reassess once triaged.
ITID-71123.priority: P2 pending triage, given containment tickets' urgency profile.
ITID-71123.escalation: Reclassify promptly to the specific applicable ITID; escalate to on-call if unclear whether isolation or release is being requested.
indicators: ServiceNow ticket that does not cleanly match isolation or release templates
vectors: Same social-engineering risk as the specific sibling leaves
rootCauses: Ambiguous or incomplete ticket submission
controls: Mandatory reclassification during triage
metrics: Volume of unclassified containment requests requiring re-triage
ITID-71123.notes: High volume here indicates the intake form needs clearer isolation-vs-release options.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Device Containment Request
playbook.description: ServiceNow-ticketed catch-all request related to device containment that does not fit a more specific subtype.

steps.title: Review ticket and classify the actual request
steps.desc: Determine whether the request is actually an isolation, a release, or another containment-related action, since it was routed as unclassified.
steps.abort: Reroute if out of scope.

steps.title: Confirm portal authentication and requestor authorization
steps.desc: Confirm the requestor is authenticated via the portal and authorized to request containment changes on the target device.
steps.abort: Reject if unauthorized.

steps.title: Gather device identifier and justification
steps.desc: Collect the exact device hostname/asset tag and the business or security justification for the requested change.
steps.abort: Return to requestor if details are missing.

steps.title: Confirm current containment state of the device
steps.desc: Record the device's current isolation status before making any change.

steps.title: Execute the appropriate containment action
steps.desc: Perform the identified action (isolate or release) via the EDR platform.
steps.abort: Escalate to endpoint team if action fails.

steps.title: Verify the device state matches the request
steps.desc: Confirm the device is now in the expected state (isolated or released) as requested.
steps.outcome: Device state confirmed to match request.

steps.title: Close ticket and notify requestor
steps.desc: Document actions taken and close the ticket.

steps.title: Flag for intake template improvement if miscategorized frequently
steps.desc: If unclassified containment tickets recur, recommend a dedicated ServiceNow catalog item to route them correctly.

ITID-71131.def: A support ticket asking the SOC or network team to block network access to a named domain identified as malicious.
ITID-71131.purpose: Captures a ServiceNow request to add a specific malicious domain to the organization's blocklist.
scopeIncludes: Requests citing threat intelligence or phishing indicators for a single domain
Requests following a confirmed malicious-link click
scopeExcludes: Bulk blocklist updates (ITID-71132)
The original malicious-activity incident that prompted the block, tracked under its own ITID
ITID-71131.severity: Low to Medium, scaling with how the domain was encountered (opportunistic scan vs. targeted phishing).
ITID-71131.priority: P3, processed same-day to limit exposure window.
ITID-71131.escalation: Escalate to threat intel if the domain is tied to an active or targeted campaign against the organization.
indicators: ServiceNow ticket citing a specific domain and source of malicious classification
vectors: N/A — this ticket classifies a defensive action, not an attack
rootCauses: Phishing email or malicious link reported by a user
Threat-intel feed identifying a new malicious domain
controls: DNS/web-proxy blocklist enforcement
Change-control review for blocklist additions affecting shared infrastructure
ITID-71131.detection: This ITID classifies the defensive blocking action; the originating malicious activity has its own detection coverage.
ITID-71131.response: Validate the domain's malicious classification via threat intel before adding; confirm block is effective.
metrics: Time from report to block
Number of domains blocked per period
ITID-71131.notes: Link to the originating incident ITID (e.g., phishing) when one exists, so the block action and root cause stay traceable.

playbook.name: Malicious Domain Blocklist Addition Request
playbook.description: ServiceNow-ticketed request to add a specific malicious domain to the enterprise blocklist.

steps.title: Review ticket and confirm portal authentication
steps.desc: Confirm the request was submitted through the authenticated portal by an authorized requestor (analyst, threat intel, or IT support).
steps.abort: Reject if unauthorized.

steps.title: Validate the domain is genuinely malicious
steps.desc: Check the domain against threat intelligence sources and/or the evidence provided (phishing email, malware C2, detection alert) to confirm it is legitimately malicious.
steps.guidance: Do not block on unverified user report alone; corroborate with at least one intel source or observed detection.
steps.outcome: Domain confirmed malicious with supporting evidence documented.
steps.abort: If evidence is inconclusive, hold the request and gather more information before blocking.

steps.title: Confirm domain's current blocklist status
steps.desc: Check whether the domain is already blocked or partially restricted to avoid duplicate or conflicting entries.

steps.title: Add domain to the blocklist
steps.desc: Add the domain to the enterprise DNS/web proxy blocklist.
steps.guidance: Include subdomains/wildcards if the evidence supports broader blocking.
steps.abort: If addition fails, escalate to network security team.

steps.title: Verify domain traffic is now blocked
steps.desc: Test resolution/access to the domain from a representative endpoint or via proxy logs to confirm the block is effective.
steps.abort: If traffic still passes, check for policy propagation delay or a bypass path (e.g. direct IP access).

steps.title: Close ticket and notify requestor
steps.desc: Document the evidence and action taken, then close the ticket and notify the requestor.

steps.title: Consider sharing indicator with threat intel feed
steps.desc: If the domain was not already known to threat intel, consider submitting it as a new indicator for broader detection.

steps.title: Check for other affected users who contacted the domain before the block
steps.desc: Search proxy/DNS logs for any users who reached the malicious domain prior to the block being applied, and route them for endpoint/security follow-up if found.
steps.guidance: Do not assume the requestor was the only party exposed; a domain report often indicates broader exposure.
steps.outcome: Affected-user search completed and any hits routed for follow-up.

ITID-71132.def: A support ticket requesting a batch addition of multiple domains — typically from a threat-intel feed or IOC list — to the organization's blocklist.
ITID-71132.purpose: Captures a ServiceNow request to add multiple malicious domains to the blocklist in a single bulk update.
scopeIncludes: Bulk updates from a curated threat-intel feed
Bulk updates following a broader campaign identifying multiple related indicators
scopeExcludes: Single-domain block requests (ITID-71131)
ITID-71132.severity: Low to Medium; bulk updates carry higher operational-impact risk if a legitimate domain is included by error.
ITID-71132.priority: P3, with careful review given the larger blast radius of a bulk change.
ITID-71132.escalation: Escalate to change management if the bulk list includes any domain used by a business-critical integration.
indicators: ServiceNow ticket referencing an IOC list or feed export with multiple domains
vectors: N/A — this ticket classifies a defensive action
rootCauses: Ingestion of a new threat-intel feed
Post-incident indicator sweep identifying multiple related domains
controls: Pre-deployment validation of bulk list against known-good domain allowlist
Rollback capability for bulk blocklist changes
ITID-71132.detection: Classifies the defensive bulk-action; not itself a detection.
ITID-71132.response: Validate the full list for false positives before deployment; monitor for unexpected business impact after applying.
metrics: Number of domains blocked per bulk update
False-positive rate in bulk blocklist additions
ITID-71132.notes: Bulk updates should go through a lighter but non-zero change-review step given the risk of accidentally blocking legitimate traffic.

playbook.name: Bulk Domain Blocklist Update Request
playbook.description: ServiceNow-ticketed request to apply a bulk list of domains to the enterprise blocklist, requiring extra care to avoid business disruption.

steps.title: Review ticket and confirm portal authentication
steps.desc: Confirm the request was submitted through the authenticated portal by an authorized requestor with permission to request bulk changes.
steps.guidance: Bulk changes typically require analyst or team-lead level authorization, not just any employee.
steps.abort: Reject if requestor lacks authority for bulk changes.

steps.title: Validate source and legitimacy of the bulk list
steps.desc: Confirm the bulk domain list originates from a credible source (threat intel feed, verified campaign IOC list) rather than an unverified export.
steps.outcome: Source of the list confirmed credible.
steps.abort: If source cannot be validated, hold the request.

steps.title: Check list for business-critical domains before bulk-applying
steps.desc: Cross-reference every domain in the bulk list against the organization's known business-critical/partner/vendor domain inventory before applying, to avoid a self-inflicted outage.
steps.guidance: This is a mandatory safety check — a bulk block that inadvertently includes a critical SaaS or partner domain can cause a major outage. Flag and remove any matches, or get explicit sign-off to proceed anyway.
steps.outcome: List confirmed clean of business-critical domains, or exceptions explicitly approved and documented.
steps.abort: If critical domains are found and cannot be resolved, exclude them from the batch or halt for stakeholder review.

steps.title: Stage the bulk update for review
steps.desc: Prepare the final, vetted domain list as a staged change prior to applying, with a documented rollback list.
steps.outcome: Staged change and rollback plan documented.

steps.title: Apply the bulk domain blocklist update
steps.desc: Push the vetted domain list to the DNS/web proxy blocklist.
steps.guidance: Apply during a low-impact window if the list is large.
steps.abort: If the platform rejects the batch or errors occur, roll back and escalate to network security team.

steps.title: Verify blocks are effective and no business disruption occurred
steps.desc: Spot-check a sample of the newly blocked domains for effectiveness, and monitor for any help desk reports of unexpected access loss.
steps.outcome: Blocks confirmed effective with no unexpected business impact.
steps.abort: If disruption is reported, immediately roll back the offending entries.

steps.title: Close ticket and notify requestor
steps.desc: Document the final applied list, exclusions made, and outcome, then close the ticket.
steps.outcome: Ticket closed with full audit trail including exclusions.

steps.title: Review bulk-update process for future automation/safety gates
steps.desc: Note whether the business-critical-domain check should be automated or if the source feed needs better pre-filtering.

ITID-71133.def: A general classification for domain-blocking support tickets submitted via ServiceNow that lack a more specific categorization.
ITID-71133.purpose: Intake bucket for ServiceNow domain-blocking requests that do not fit the single or bulk sibling leaves.
scopeIncludes: Any ServiceNow domain-block request not otherwise classified
scopeExcludes: Requests clearly matching ITID-71131 (single) or ITID-71132 (bulk)
ITID-71133.severity: Low by default; reassess once triaged.
ITID-71133.escalation: Reclassify to the specific applicable ITID once the scope of the request is clear.
indicators: ServiceNow ticket that does not cleanly match single or bulk block templates
vectors: N/A
rootCauses: Ambiguous or incomplete ticket submission
controls: Mandatory reclassification during triage
metrics: Volume of unclassified domain-block requests
ITID-71133.notes: Persistent volume here suggests the intake form needs a single-vs-bulk selector.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Domain Blocking Request
playbook.description: ServiceNow-ticketed catch-all request related to domain blocking that does not fit a more specific subtype.

steps.title: Review ticket and classify the actual request
steps.desc: Determine whether the request is a single-domain block, bulk block, or another blocking-related action, since it was routed as unclassified.
steps.abort: Reroute if out of scope.

steps.title: Confirm portal authentication and requestor authorization
steps.desc: Confirm the requestor is authenticated via the portal and authorized to request blocklist changes.
steps.abort: Reject if unauthorized.

steps.title: Gather domain(s) and justification
steps.desc: Collect the exact domain(s) and the reason/evidence supporting the block.
steps.abort: Return to requestor if details are missing.

steps.title: Confirm current blocklist status of the domain(s)
steps.desc: Check whether the domain(s) are already blocked to avoid duplicate entries.

steps.title: Apply the domain block
steps.desc: Add the domain(s) to the DNS/web proxy blocklist.
steps.abort: Escalate to network security team if action fails.

steps.title: Verify block is effective
steps.desc: Confirm the domain(s) are no longer reachable as expected.

steps.title: Close ticket and notify requestor
steps.desc: Document actions taken and close the ticket.

steps.title: Flag for intake template improvement if miscategorized frequently
steps.desc: If unclassified blocking tickets recur, recommend a dedicated ServiceNow catalog item to route them correctly.

ITID-71141.def: A support ticket asking that a specific domain be unblocked, on the grounds that it was incorrectly classified as malicious.
ITID-71141.purpose: Captures a ServiceNow request to remove a domain from the blocklist because it was blocked in error.
scopeIncludes: Requests citing evidence that a domain is legitimate/benign
Requests where a blocklist source is shown to have misclassified the domain
scopeExcludes: Business-justified allowlist exceptions for a known-risky domain (ITID-71142)
ITID-71141.severity: Low; the primary risk is business disruption from an over-broad block rather than a security concern.
ITID-71141.priority: P3, prioritized when the block is actively disrupting a business function.
ITID-71141.escalation: Escalate to threat intel to correct the source classification if the false-positive pattern recurs.
indicators: ServiceNow ticket disputing a block with supporting evidence of legitimacy
vectors: An attacker registering a domain designed to closely resemble a legitimate one, then requesting it be unblocked under false pretenses — verify domain identity carefully
rootCauses: Overbroad threat-intel classification
Shared hosting infrastructure causing collateral blocking of an unrelated legitimate domain
controls: Independent verification of domain legitimacy before unblocking
Feedback loop to the threat-intel source on confirmed false positives
ITID-71141.detection: Classifies the unblock request; not itself a detection.
ITID-71141.response: Verify legitimacy independently before unblocking; do not unblock solely on requester assertion.
metrics: False-positive block rate
Time to resolve unblock requests
ITID-71141.notes: Distinguish carefully from ITID-71142: this leaf is for genuine misclassification, not a business exception for a domain that remains genuinely risky.

playbook.name: False-Positive Domain Unblock Request
playbook.description: ServiceNow-ticketed request to unblock a domain believed to be incorrectly flagged as malicious, requiring independent confirmation before unblocking.

steps.title: Review ticket and confirm portal authentication
steps.desc: Confirm the request was submitted through the authenticated portal by an authorized requestor.
steps.abort: Reject if unauthorized.

steps.title: Independently review the original block reason
steps.desc: Pull the original blocking rationale (threat intel hit, detection alert, prior incident) and evaluate the evidence yourself rather than accepting the requestor's claim that it's a false positive.
steps.guidance: Check whether the domain still resolves to known-malicious infrastructure, has changed ownership, or was blocked as part of a broader campaign block.
steps.outcome: Analyst independently confirms whether the block was truly a false positive.
steps.abort: If evidence still supports the block being valid, deny the unblock request and explain why.

steps.title: Gather business justification for access
steps.desc: Document why the requestor needs access to this domain.

steps.title: Confirm domain remains blocked pending review
steps.desc: Ensure the block stays in place while the false-positive review is conducted.
steps.outcome: Block state confirmed unchanged pending eradication.

steps.title: Remove domain from the blocklist
steps.desc: Remove the domain entry from the DNS/web proxy blocklist once confirmed as a genuine false positive.
steps.abort: If removal fails, escalate to network security team.

steps.title: Verify domain access is restored
steps.desc: Confirm the domain is now reachable as expected from a representative endpoint.
steps.abort: If still blocked, check for a duplicate rule or overlapping policy.

steps.title: Close ticket and notify requestor
steps.desc: Document the review findings and action taken, then close the ticket.

steps.title: Track false-positive rate for the blocking source
steps.desc: Log this instance against the threat intel feed or rule that caused the erroneous block; recommend tuning if false positives recur from the same source.
steps.outcome: False-positive instance logged; tuning recommendation raised if pattern threshold met.

ITID-71142.def: A support ticket requesting that a domain be unblocked or allowlisted for a specific business need, despite retaining a risk classification.
ITID-71142.purpose: Captures a ServiceNow request for a business-justified exception to allow access to a domain that remains classified as risky.
scopeIncludes: Requests for time-bound access to a domain needed for a specific vendor integration or research purpose
scopeExcludes: Requests asserting the domain was misclassified entirely (ITID-71141)
ITID-71142.severity: Medium, since the domain's risk classification is not being disputed — only the business need is being weighed against it.
ITID-71142.priority: P3, requires risk-acceptance sign-off before processing.
ITID-71142.escalation: Escalate to a risk owner or manager for formal risk acceptance before granting the exception.
indicators: ServiceNow ticket including business justification and a named risk-accepting approver
vectors: An attacker or insider using a fabricated business justification to gain access to a genuinely malicious domain
rootCauses: Legitimate third-party service hosted on infrastructure that also hosts known-risky content
controls: Formal risk-acceptance workflow with named approver
Time-bound exception with automatic expiry and review
ITID-71142.detection: Classifies the exception request; not itself a detection.
ITID-71142.response: Require documented risk acceptance; set an expiry date and monitor traffic to the allowlisted domain during the exception period.
metrics: Number of active risk exceptions
Overdue exceptions past their review date
ITID-71142.notes: Every exception granted here should carry a hard expiry — indefinite exceptions defeat the purpose of the underlying block.

playbook.name: Business-Justified Domain Allowlist Exception Request
playbook.description: ServiceNow-ticketed request to allowlist a currently-blocked domain for a documented business reason, requiring risk sign-off and a time-bound exception.

steps.title: Review ticket and confirm portal authentication
steps.desc: Confirm the request was submitted through the authenticated portal by an authorized requestor.
steps.abort: Reject if unauthorized.

steps.title: Confirm the domain is still validly blocked and understand why
steps.desc: Review why the domain is currently blocked (this is not a false-positive claim — the block may be legitimate but business needs an exception).

steps.title: Gather business justification and scope
steps.desc: Document the specific business need, which users/systems require access, and the requested duration.
steps.abort: If justification is insufficient, return to requestor for more detail.

steps.title: Obtain risk-acceptance sign-off
steps.desc: Route the exception request to the appropriate risk owner (security manager or CISO delegate) for formal sign-off, since this overrides a security control.
steps.guidance: Do not proceed without documented approval from someone authorized to accept the residual risk of allowing access to a known-risky domain.
steps.abort: If sign-off is denied, close the request as declined and notify the requestor.

steps.title: Confirm domain remains blocked pending approval
steps.desc: Ensure the block stays active until sign-off is obtained.
steps.outcome: Block state confirmed unchanged pending eradication.

steps.title: Apply a scoped, time-bound allowlist exception
steps.desc: Add a narrowly-scoped allowlist entry (limited to the specific users/systems and domain path if possible) with an explicit expiry date tied to the approved duration.
steps.guidance: Avoid a blanket, permanent allowlist entry; set a calendar reminder or automated expiry for review.
steps.outcome: Time-bound exception applied with documented expiry.
steps.abort: If the platform cannot enforce scoping/expiry, document a manual review date and proceed with heightened monitoring.

steps.title: Verify access works for the intended scope only
steps.desc: Confirm the domain is reachable for the approved users/systems and remains blocked for everyone else.
steps.outcome: Scoped access confirmed working as intended.
steps.abort: If the exception is too broad, tighten the scope.

steps.title: Close ticket and notify requestor of expiry date
steps.desc: Document the approval, scope, and expiry date, then close the ticket and notify the requestor of when the exception will lapse.
steps.outcome: Ticket closed with full audit trail including expiry.

steps.title: Schedule exception expiry review
steps.desc: Ensure the exception is tracked for review/removal at expiry rather than becoming a permanent, forgotten gap.
steps.guidance: Recommend a periodic audit of all active domain exceptions.

ITID-71143.def: A general classification for domain-unblocking support tickets submitted via ServiceNow that lack a more specific categorization.
ITID-71143.purpose: Intake bucket for ServiceNow domain-unblocking requests that do not fit the false-positive or exception sibling leaves.
scopeIncludes: Any ServiceNow domain-unblock request not otherwise classified
scopeExcludes: Requests clearly matching ITID-71141 (false-positive) or ITID-71142 (business exception)
ITID-71143.severity: Low by default; reassess once triaged.
ITID-71143.escalation: Reclassify to the specific applicable ITID once the nature of the request is clear.
indicators: ServiceNow ticket that does not cleanly match false-positive or exception templates
vectors: Same social-engineering risk as the specific sibling leaves
rootCauses: Ambiguous or incomplete ticket submission
controls: Mandatory reclassification during triage
metrics: Volume of unclassified domain-unblock requests
ITID-71143.notes: Persistent volume here suggests the intake form needs clearer false-positive-vs-exception options.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Domain Unblocking Request
playbook.description: ServiceNow-ticketed catch-all request related to domain unblocking that does not fit a more specific subtype.

steps.title: Review ticket and classify the actual request
steps.desc: Determine whether the request is a false-positive unblock, a business-justified exception, or another unblocking-related action, since it was routed as unclassified.
steps.abort: Reroute if out of scope.

steps.title: Confirm portal authentication and requestor authorization
steps.desc: Confirm the requestor is authenticated via the portal and authorized to request unblocking.
steps.abort: Reject if unauthorized.

steps.title: Review original block reason and gather justification
steps.desc: Check why the domain was blocked and collect the requestor's justification for unblocking.
steps.guidance: Do not unblock without understanding the original reason for the block.
steps.abort: If block reason indicates active threat, deny the request.

steps.title: Confirm domain remains blocked pending review
steps.desc: Ensure the block stays active while the request is processed.
steps.outcome: Block state confirmed unchanged pending eradication.

steps.title: Execute the appropriate unblocking action
steps.desc: Remove the domain from the blocklist or apply a scoped exception per the classified request type.
steps.abort: Escalate to network security team if action fails.

steps.title: Verify domain access matches the request
steps.desc: Confirm the domain is now accessible as intended.

steps.title: Close ticket and notify requestor
steps.desc: Document actions taken and close the ticket.

steps.title: Flag for intake template improvement if miscategorized frequently
steps.desc: If unclassified unblocking tickets recur, recommend a dedicated ServiceNow catalog item to route them correctly.

ITID-71151.def: A support ticket requesting that a user or team be granted access to a named security tool, such as a SIEM dashboard or EDR console.
ITID-71151.purpose: Captures a ServiceNow request for access to a specific security tool or dashboard.
scopeIncludes: New-hire access requests for SOC tooling
Requests to expand an existing user's tool permissions
scopeExcludes: Access requests for non-security business applications (handled by general IT access management)
ITID-71151.severity: Low; the risk is proportional to the privilege level of the tool being requested.
ITID-71151.priority: P4, routine, escalating to P3 for requests involving administrative-level tool access.
ITID-71151.escalation: Escalate to the tool owner for approval when the requested access includes administrative or configuration privileges.
indicators: ServiceNow ticket naming a specific security tool and requested permission level
vectors: An attacker with a compromised employee account requesting elevated access to security tooling to surveil or evade detection
rootCauses: Legitimate onboarding or role-change access need
controls: Manager and tool-owner approval workflow
Periodic access review/recertification for security-tool permissions
ITID-71151.detection: Intake classification for the access request; not itself a detection.
ITID-71151.response: Verify business justification and manager approval before granting; apply least-privilege by default.
metrics: Access requests granted per period
Percentage of grants matching least-privilege baseline
ITID-71151.notes: Access to security tooling itself is a sensitive privilege — treat requests here with the same rigor as any privileged-access grant.

playbook.name: General Security Tooling Access Request
playbook.description: ServiceNow-ticketed request from an internal analyst for temporary or standing access to a security tool or console.

steps.title: Review ticket and confirm portal authentication
steps.desc: Confirm the request was submitted through the authenticated portal.
steps.abort: Reject if unauthenticated.

steps.title: Verify requestor's role and need-to-know for the tool
steps.desc: Confirm the requestor's team/role justifies access to the specific tool requested, and that the access level requested matches their responsibilities.
steps.guidance: Cross-check against the requestor's manager or team lead if the need is unclear.
steps.outcome: Role and need-to-know confirmed appropriate for the requested access.
steps.abort: If need cannot be established, deny or scope down the request.

steps.title: Determine access scope and duration
steps.desc: Document whether access should be permanent (role-based) or temporary (project/investigation-based) and the appropriate permission level.

steps.title: Confirm current access state
steps.desc: Check whether the requestor already has partial or conflicting access before granting new access.

steps.title: Grant the requested tool access
steps.desc: Provision the access in the relevant security tool/console at the scoped permission level.
steps.guidance: Set an expiry for temporary access grants.
steps.abort: Escalate to tool administrator if provisioning fails.

steps.title: Confirm access is working for the requestor
steps.desc: Have the requestor confirm they can log in and use the tool as needed.
steps.abort: If access does not work, re-check provisioning and permission mappings.

steps.title: Close ticket and notify requestor
steps.desc: Document the grant details (scope, duration, approver) and close the ticket.

steps.title: Flag recurring ad-hoc access requests as a process/tooling gap
steps.desc: If requests for this tool/access type recur frequently from the same team, recommend a standing role-based access policy instead of one-off tickets.
steps.outcome: Process-improvement note logged if a pattern is identified.

ITID-71152.def: A support ticket asking the SOC to provide investigative assistance — such as a log pull or IOC lookup — for an informal or preliminary inquiry.
ITID-71152.purpose: Captures a ServiceNow request for ad-hoc SOC support on an investigation not already tracked as its own incident.
scopeIncludes: Requests for a one-off log search or artifact review
Requests supporting an HR or legal inquiry with a security component
scopeExcludes: Requests that are clearly part of an already-opened formal incident (tracked under that incident's own ITID)
ITID-71152.severity: Low to Medium, depending on the sensitivity of the underlying inquiry (e.g., HR investigations warrant discretion).
ITID-71152.priority: P3, timeline driven by the requesting party's own urgency.
ITID-71152.escalation: Escalate to a formal incident if the investigation support request surfaces evidence of an active security incident.
indicators: ServiceNow ticket requesting log pulls, artifact reviews, or IOC lookups outside a formal incident
vectors: N/A — this is a request classification, not an attack
rootCauses: Preliminary inquiry before a decision is made to open a formal case
controls: Chain-of-custody handling for any evidence pulled, in case it later supports a formal case or HR/legal action
ITID-71152.detection: Intake classification for the support request; not itself a detection.
ITID-71152.response: Handle with appropriate discretion, especially for HR-related requests; preserve evidence integrity in case of later escalation.
metrics: Ad-hoc investigation requests processed per period
Percentage that escalate to formal incidents
ITID-71152.notes: If this request repeatedly surfaces evidence of a pattern (not a one-off), consider whether a formal investigation should be opened proactively.

playbook.name: Ad-Hoc Investigation Support Request
playbook.description: ServiceNow-ticketed request from a fellow analyst for temporary case support or investigative assistance on an active matter.

steps.title: Review ticket and confirm portal authentication
steps.desc: Confirm the request was submitted through the authenticated portal.
steps.abort: Reject if unauthenticated.

steps.title: Verify requestor's role and need-to-know for the case
steps.desc: Confirm the requesting analyst is actually assigned to or authorized to involve support on the referenced case/investigation.
steps.guidance: Check the case management system for the requestor's association with the case before providing any details or access.
steps.abort: If the requestor has no documented tie to the case, deny and direct them to the case owner.

steps.title: Scope the specific support needed
steps.desc: Document exactly what support is being requested (data pull, second-analyst review, tool run, escalation help).

steps.title: Confirm case status before providing support
steps.desc: Check the current state/priority of the referenced case to ensure support is applied appropriately.

steps.title: Provide the requested investigative support
steps.desc: Perform the scoped support activity (e.g. run a query, provide temporary case access, review evidence).
steps.abort: If the support requires access beyond your authority, escalate to a senior analyst or team lead.

steps.title: Confirm the support met the requestor's need
steps.desc: Check with the requesting analyst that the assistance resolved their need for the case.
steps.outcome: Requestor confirms the support was sufficient.
steps.abort: If not sufficient, clarify remaining need and continue or escalate.

steps.title: Close ticket and notify requestor
steps.desc: Document the support provided and close the ticket, ensuring the action is also logged against the underlying case if applicable.
steps.outcome: Ticket closed with audit trail; case notes updated if relevant.

steps.title: Flag recurring ad-hoc support requests as a process/tooling gap
steps.desc: If this type of ad-hoc support request recurs often (e.g. the same data pull repeatedly requested), recommend a self-service tool or standard runbook to reduce ticket volume.
steps.outcome: Process-improvement note logged if a pattern is identified.

ITID-71153.def: A general classification for ServiceNow tickets submitted to the SOC that fall outside account-unlock, containment, domain-blocking, and investigation-support categories.
ITID-71153.purpose: Intake bucket for miscellaneous ServiceNow SOC requests that do not fit any other operational-request leaf.
scopeIncludes: Any ServiceNow SOC request not otherwise classified
scopeExcludes: Requests clearly matching any other Service Now Tickets sibling leaf
ITID-71153.severity: Low by default; reassess once triaged.
ITID-71153.escalation: Reclassify to the specific applicable ITID or open a new categorization if a recurring pattern is identified.
indicators: ServiceNow ticket that does not match any of the templated request types
vectors: N/A
rootCauses: Novel or infrequent request type not yet formally categorized
controls: Periodic review of this bucket to identify candidates for new formal categories
ITID-71153.response: Triage promptly; escalate to taxonomy owners if a recurring request type should become its own ITID.
metrics: Volume of miscellaneous requests
Recurring request types identified for future formal categorization
ITID-71153.notes: This is the general catch-all for the ServiceNow channel — high or growing volume here signals a taxonomy gap.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Miscellaneous ServiceNow Request
playbook.description: ServiceNow-ticketed catch-all miscellaneous request that does not fit password/device/domain categories.

steps.title: Review ticket and confirm portal authentication
steps.desc: Confirm the request was submitted through the authenticated portal.
steps.abort: Reject if unauthenticated.

steps.title: Clarify the specific nature of the request
steps.desc: Since the request is miscellaneous/unclassified, engage the requestor to pin down exactly what action or information is needed.
steps.outcome: Request understood in concrete, actionable terms.
steps.abort: If the request is out of scope for the SOC, reroute to the correct team.

steps.title: Verify requestor authorization for the specific ask
steps.desc: Confirm the requestor has standing to make this particular request based on role/need.
steps.abort: Deny if authorization cannot be established.

steps.title: Confirm current state relevant to the request
steps.desc: Document the baseline state of whatever system/account/data is involved before acting.

steps.title: Execute the requested miscellaneous action
steps.desc: Carry out the specific action clarified in identification.
steps.abort: Escalate if the action requires authority or tooling outside the SOC's standard scope.

steps.title: Verify the outcome meets the request
steps.desc: Confirm with the requestor that the action resolved their need.

steps.title: Close ticket and notify requestor
steps.desc: Document actions taken and close the ticket.

steps.title: Flag for intake template improvement if a pattern emerges
steps.desc: If a specific type of 'miscellaneous' request recurs often, recommend creating a dedicated ServiceNow catalog item for it.
steps.outcome: Process-improvement note logged if a pattern is identified.

ITID-71211.def: An unlock or risk-dismissal support request received directly through instant messaging, outside the formal ServiceNow ticketing workflow.
ITID-71211.purpose: Captures a request for account unlock or risk-alert dismissal submitted via an instant-messaging channel (e.g., Slack/Teams) rather than a formal ticket.
scopeIncludes: Direct messages or channel posts to the SOC asking for an account unlock or alert dismissal
scopeExcludes: The equivalent request submitted via ServiceNow (ITID-71111/71112) or email (ITID-71311)
ITID-71211.severity: Medium — the informal channel carries a higher identity-verification risk than a ticketing system with built-in authentication.
ITID-71211.priority: P3; process promptly but only after identity verification.
ITID-71211.escalation: Escalate to a formal ticket and verify identity through an independent channel before acting on any IM-based request.
indicators: Direct message to a SOC channel or individual analyst requesting an unlock or dismissal
vectors: Impersonation of an employee or executive via a spoofed or compromised messaging account to socially engineer an unlock (a known real-world tactic given IM's lower built-in verification)
rootCauses: User preference for a faster, informal channel over the ticketing system
controls: Mandatory out-of-band identity verification for any IM-based account action request
Policy requiring IM requests to be converted into a formal ticket before action
ITID-71211.detection: Instant-messaging channels generally lack the built-in identity assurance of a ticketing system — treat with elevated scrutiny.
ITID-71211.response: Do not act on the IM request directly; verify identity out-of-band and log the action against a formal ticket.
metrics: IM-channel requests requiring escalated verification
Confirmed impersonation attempts via IM
ITID-71211.notes: The MITRE mapping here reflects the impersonation risk inherent to the IM channel, not the routine legitimate request itself — most IM requests are genuine, but the channel's lower assurance warrants the same technique awareness as ITID-71111/71112.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Password Unlock or Risk Dismissal Request (Instant Messaging Channel)
playbook.description: Instant-messaging request to unlock an account or dismiss a risk alert, a high-risk channel requiring independent identity verification before any action.

steps.title: Record the IM request and flag as high-risk channel
steps.desc: Log the IM conversation (handle, timestamp, exact request) and flag it as arriving via a channel that can be spoofed or compromised.
steps.guidance: IM handles/accounts can be impersonated or taken over; treat every IM-only request with elevated scrutiny.
steps.outcome: Request logged with channel risk flagged.

steps.title: Verify identity via an independent second channel before acting
steps.desc: Before taking any action, verify the requestor's identity through a separate, independent channel — e.g. call the person's known phone number on file, or confirm with their manager — do not rely on the IM conversation alone, even if the handle looks familiar.
steps.guidance: This is mandatory for this channel. Never act on an IM-only request without this independent confirmation, since IM accounts can be compromised or spoofed.
steps.outcome: Requestor identity confirmed via an independent, out-of-band method.
steps.abort: If independent verification cannot be completed or raises doubt, do not act — ask the requestor to submit via ServiceNow instead.

steps.title: Confirm requestor authorization for the specific account
steps.desc: After identity is confirmed, verify the requestor is the account owner or an authorized delegate.
steps.abort: Reject if authorization cannot be established.

steps.title: Determine specific action and gather details
steps.desc: Clarify whether this is an unlock, a risk dismissal, or both, and gather the account identifier and reason.
steps.guidance: For risk dismissal, independently review the underlying alert rather than accepting the requestor's claim.

steps.title: Confirm account remains in current state pending verification
steps.desc: Ensure no action is taken until both identity and authorization checks are fully complete.
steps.outcome: Account state confirmed unchanged pending eradication.

steps.title: Execute the unlock or risk dismissal
steps.desc: Perform the verified action in Active Directory / identity risk console.
steps.abort: Escalate to IAM if action fails.

steps.title: Verify resolution and confirm via the independent channel
steps.desc: Confirm the user can log in normally, and notify them of completion via the same independent channel used for verification (not just IM).
steps.outcome: Resolution confirmed and requestor notified via a trusted channel.

steps.title: Document the interaction and close out
steps.desc: Create/update a ticket record documenting the IM request, the independent verification method used, and the action taken, since IM itself is not an auditable system of record.
steps.outcome: Full record created in the ticketing system for audit purposes.

steps.title: Reinforce channel policy if IM-originated requests recur
steps.desc: If IM-based requests for this action type are frequent, consider reminding staff to use the ServiceNow portal directly, and monitor for social-engineering attempts via IM.

ITID-71221.def: A request to isolate or release a device from network containment, received directly through instant messaging outside the formal ServiceNow workflow.
ITID-71221.purpose: Captures a device-containment request submitted via an instant-messaging channel rather than a formal ticket.
scopeIncludes: Urgent containment requests posted directly to a SOC IM channel
scopeExcludes: The equivalent request submitted via ServiceNow (ITID-71121/71122) or email (ITID-71321)
ITID-71221.severity: Medium to High, consistent with the underlying containment urgency, with added identity-verification risk from the informal channel.
ITID-71221.priority: P2; the urgency of containment requests generally justifies fast action, but identity should still be confirmed for release requests.
ITID-71221.escalation: Escalate immediately for isolation requests (err toward containing); require stronger verification before honoring a release request received via IM.
indicators: Direct message to a SOC channel requesting isolation or release of a named device
vectors: An adversary attempting to have a genuinely compromised device released from containment via a fabricated IM request
rootCauses: Analyst or manager preference for fast, informal communication during an active incident
controls: Formal ticket creation to backstop any IM-driven containment action
Sign-off requirement for release requests regardless of channel
ITID-71221.detection: Intake classification; the underlying suspected compromise (if any) has its own detection coverage.
ITID-71221.response: Act quickly on isolation requests; require verification and sign-off before honoring release requests made via IM.
metrics: IM-channel containment requests processed
